checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and what was already reviewed at the last IDT, so only changes since then are surfaced.
Falls and near-falls: count, circumstances, injuries, and any fall-related ED visit, given the new osteoporosis diagnosis (onset 2026-06-23) and age 80 on clopidogrel.
ED visits and hospital admissions in the window, with reasons, discharge summaries, and any readmission.

Medication changes: new starts, stops, dose changes, and refills missed since last review. Current list shows only metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin spray, and simvastatin; verify this list is complete, since no diabetes, blood pressure, or bone-health agents appear despite listed type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and osteoporosis.

Osteoporosis follow-up: whether a treatment plan, calcium/vitamin D status, DXA result, and fracture-risk discussion were documented after the 2026-06-23 diagnosis, and whether any bone-health medication was prescribed or declined.
Glycemic control: most recent HbA1c, fasting and random glucose trends, hypoglycemia episodes, and whether the diabetes plan and monitoring frequency are current.
Blood pressure trend: home and clinic readings, orthostatic readings if dizziness or falls occurred, and any changes to antihypertensive therapy.

Kidney function: latest eGFR, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and potassium, given CKD stages 1 and 2 with diabetic kidney disease and microalbuminuria; check for any new nephrotoxic or renally relevant medications.

Cardiac status: chest pain or nitroglycerin use frequency, recent cardiology contact, lipid panel and statin adherence, and antiplatelet bleeding events, given ischemic heart disease and anemia history.
Anemia and bleeding: latest hemoglobin and iron studies, any bleeding or bruising on clopidogrel, and whether anemia workup is current.

Weight and BMI trend (obesity, metabolic syndrome), appetite changes, and any dietitian or nutrition follow-up; dental status given loss of teeth and its effect on intake; neuropathy symptoms and foot exam status; function and ADLs/IADLs compared with prior assessment; cognition and mood screen results and social engagement; caregiver situation and any change in support; and PACE service attendance (day center, therapies, transport) plus any due care-plan items, assessments, or reassessments falling in the window.
